beats.title:
What if California got
30 days of extreme rain?
beats.caption:
At first, everyone celebrates.
Then the water keeps rising

stat.label:
a storm sequence scientists
simulated in a 2022 study

beats.visual: Night-blue globe. A glowing moisture plume streams from near Hawaii to California within 2 s.

camera.reason: Shows where in the world the water comes from

beats.point: 1 · The rain feels like a gift
beats.caption:
Atmospheric rivers bring about **30–50%**
of West Coast precipitation

stat.label:
of yearly West Coast
precipitation · NOAA

beats.visual: Fly-to: the camera follows the plume down through the cloud deck and emerges over the California relief map.

camera.shot: Fly-to: zoom in along the plume, cloud pass, settle over California
camera.reason: Carries the viewer from the Pacific source to the destination

beats.point: 1 · The rain feels like a gift
beats.caption:
Reservoirs rise fast. Shasta Lake
can hold **4.55 million** acre-feet

stat.label:
acre-feet: Shasta Lake's capacity
1 acre-foot ≈ 326,000 gallons · USBR

beats.visual: Real-terrain diorama of Shasta Lake. The shoreline climbs the canyons while dry grey hills turn green.

camera.shot: Slow push-in toward Shasta Dam and the rising shoreline
camera.reason: Lets the viewer watch the waterline creep up

beats.caption:
Winter 2022–23 brought **9** atmospheric
rivers in just 3 weeks
beats.visual: Cut-away block of hillside. Rain falls in pulses and the soil cross-section fills with water from the top down.

camera.shot: Slow push-in on the soil cross-section
camera.reason: Builds tension as the soil runs out of room

beats.caption:
Soaked slopes can slide. That winter,
**700+** landslides were reported
beats.visual: Runoff sheets downhill into the creek and street. Slide-prone slope outlined in amber; a small empty-hillside slump.

camera.reason: Shows the slope in 3d and where the water goes

beats.point: 3 · Parts of the valley could become a lake
beats.caption:
Sierra runoff pours into one valley,
about **400 miles** long

stat.label: length of the Central Valley · USGS

beats.visual: Visual reset to the state relief map. Flow pulses run down Sierra rivers into the Sacramento and San Joaquin.

camera.shot: Crane up from the Sierra slopes to the whole valley
camera.reason: 'It keeps going': reveals how much land drains to one place

beats.point: 3 · Parts of the valley could become a lake
beats.caption:
About **1,600 miles** of levees strain
to hold the rivers

stat.label:
of levees in the State Plan
of Flood Control · DWR

beats.visual: Push-in on the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta. Levee lines glow amber as rivers rise against them.

camera.reason: Tension: the pressure point of the whole system

beats.point: 3 · Parts of the valley could become a lake
beats.caption:
In a USGS megastorm scenario, floods
stretch **300 miles** down the valley

stat.label:
of modeled flooding, 20+ miles wide
USGS ARkStorm scenario

beats.visual: Biggest visual. Separate flooded patches spread from the rivers and join into one long inland sea, reaching the Tulare Lake basin.

camera.shot: Top-down crane up (pull back) along the whole valley
camera.reason: 'It keeps going': the flood outgrows the frame

beats.tag: Illustrative scenario, not a flood model

beats.point: 4 · The effects reach your everyday life
beats.caption:
In early 2023, PG&E restored power
to **2 million+** customers

stat.label:
customers' power restored,
Dec 30 2022 – Jan 10 2023 · PG&E

beats.visual: A delivery truck leaves a valley farm. Ahead, a flooded highway (amber barrier) and a power line with an amber outage glow.

camera.shot: Tracking dolly along the delivery route
camera.reason: Follows one trip so the impact feels personal

beats.point: 4 · The effects reach your everyday life
beats.caption:
About **25%** of America's food comes
from the Central Valley
beats.visual: The detoured route crosses the mountains to a Los Angeles grocery store whose produce shelf has amber gaps.

camera.shot: Continue the dolly south, then push in on the store
camera.reason: Lands the ripple at the viewer's own grocery store

beats.caption:
In 2023, California recharged about
**4.1 million** acre-feet underground

stat.label:
acre-feet of managed recharge,
water year 2023 · DWR

beats.visual: Clouds part, light warms. One side: a muddy town mid-cleanup. Other side: a gate sends floodwater into a recharge basin; the aquifer below fills green.

camera.shot: Crane down from the basin into the cross-section
camera.reason: Follows the water underground, where it becomes useful

beats.title:
California has seen
something like this before
beats.caption:
In 1861–62, about **45 days** of storms
flooded the Sacramento Valley

stat.label:
of storms. The state capital moved
to San Francisco, Jan–May 1862

beats.visual: Low hero angle on an 1860s river town diorama, water up to the first floors, an empty rowboat tied to a porch.

camera.reason: Gives the history its weight: the big reveal

beats.title:
Thirty days of rain
could change California
beats.caption:
How we make room for water
changes what happens next

stat.label:
of basins soak Santa Ana River
water into the ground · OCWD

beats.visual: Warm light over Southern California: the Santa Ana River watershed glows, recharge basins turn green, then the camera rises to the whole state.

camera.shot: Crane up from the Santa Ana basins to the whole state
camera.reason: Ends wide and open: the choice is statewide

beats.endCard:
California's next big investment:
more water storage—or more room
for rivers?
beats.visual: The scene dims behind a large neutral question.

camera.reason: Gives the question room to land
